key_insight: An LLM can directly write effective variational quantum circuit parameters without optimizer feedback when the parameter space has interpretable structure.
engineering_relevance: LLM-written parameters could reduce costly quantum-device optimization evaluations, either as direct solutions or as strong optimizer warm starts.
method: Provide the LLM with the problem, circuit, and gate conventions.
Execute its parameters unchanged, without loss, gradient, or accuracy feedback.
Compare against random parameters, classical optimization, and LLM-initialized optimization on the same circuits.
evidence_signal: Across 139 requests spanning digit classification, VQE, and MaxCut QAOA, the authors report 93–96% accuracy on digits 3 versus 8 and warm-start optimization reaching its best value after a median of one evaluation rather than hundreds.
watch_item: Reliability depends on parameter interpretability and gate conventions: fixed circuits exceeding 30 weights fell to chance classification accuracy, and 6 of 42 QAOA replies used incorrect mixing-angle signs.
paper_title: Weight-Space Programming of Variational Quantum Circuits: Large Language Models Write Quantum Circuit Parameters Without an Optimizer
